text:
A speech expert has set out why Donald Trump might be suffering from a baffling physical symptom



(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A speech expert has explained why Donald Trump might be experiencing a puzzling physical symptom described as "glitches". The US President's cognitive health has become a major topic of discussion during his second term, driven partly by his meandering speeches, unpredictable conduct and apparent difficulty remaining awake.

Additionally, his physical health has come under scrutiny. Commentators have highlighted symptoms including a bruised hand, neck rash, and swollen ankles as potential indicators of Trump's deteriorating health.

Trump has dismissed such claims regarding his mental acuity, maintaining he "aced" three cognitive tests. Nevertheless, one vocal critic has drawn attention to another "physical thing" that seemingly contradicts his assertions. It comes after Trump's aides allegedly "rushed the press" out of the Oval Office after one of his speeches raised concerns that "something was wrong".

David Pakman has pointed to what he described as a "physical thing"

David Pakman showcased footage of the alleged "glitches" on his YouTube channel, The David Pakman Show. He stated: "We've observed in Donald Trump what appears to be a diminished range of vocabulary, that the sort of number of words he uses has diminished over time.

"We've seen these...What I call glitches, where when he gets a word wrong, there's a physical thing where a shoulder goes up and he seems to almost reboot, for lack of a better term."

He presented his observations to speech-language pathologist Hilary Shae, who specialises in concussions and neurological disorders. He inquired, as a "layperson", whether he was creating "something out of nothing" or if there were "clinically relevant" insights to be gained.

Hilary confirmed he was "on target". She said: "So, with that question, I actually want to separate out twitches and glitches because there's two different things going on. And then when they occur at the same time, there's a reason.

President Donald Trump during a speech(Image: Getty)

"So the twitches are something likely that...they're likely something that's called myoclonus. And a myoclonus is going to be a brief burst of an involuntary muscle movement.

"So that's where you see kind of the arm go out, the shoulder go up, kind of whatever. What's happening within the brain networks is that the brain is supposed to be regulating and suppressing unwanted motor movements.

"If you think about kids, they're all over the place. Their brains haven't developed enough to do this. And then, kind of as we age, and the brain declines, it comes back. So the frontal lobe should be suppressing unwanted motor movements like those twitches. That's called inhibitory control or disinhibition."

Hilary explained that cognitive decline and dementia "damages the circuits", leading to what she described as an "excitatory 'go do this' inhibitory stop", followed by "cortical excitability."

She characterised this as the brain's neurones becoming "hyperexcitable", which leads to "sudden muscle contractions". Hilary then set out the explanation of "glitch".

She continued: "So the word glitch, that has to do with where the brain's energy is going; the brain's energy is going to the glitch. The glitch is its own separate issue, a language difficulty, phonemic paraphasia.

"So, because the brain is already struggling to suppress these movements, now all of a sudden it's putting a lot more effort to this speech because there was an error."

Hilary said the brain has to think how it can "correct" the problem or how to "get out" of the situation, and that the twitches then happen "more frequently."
